name: Trinidad and Tobago

findings.summary: bmobile (TSTT) launched Trinidad and Tobago's first 5G service, a fixed wireless network built with Huawei, with a first phase covering Port of Spain, San Fernando, Point Lisas, Arima and industrial and campus zones.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor rule: Huawei supplies the 5G FWA network, so pole prc. Tier 5 for a launched commercial service, though described as a limited first phase. A Dec 2020 Express report says TSTT will also use Huawei 5G at Phoenix Park Industrial Estate, a park financed by a US$104.3m China Exim concessional loan; not coded separately. Huawei supply of TSTT 4G/core not established. Corroboration: operator release (S1) plus independent newspaper report. Not reconfirmed as current in 2026.

findings.summary: Ericsson deployed Digicel's Evolved HSPA network in Trinidad and Tobago using RBS 6000 multi-standard radio base stations, with design, integration and deployment services; the network went live in 2012.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson (Sweden) is the RAN vendor, so pole third. Core vendor not stated. Pre-2020 and not reconfirmed; Digicel's 2018 LTE upgrade release names no vendor, so current RAN supplier is unverified. Single opened S2 source, so low.

findings.local_actor: Government of Trinidad and Tobago (Office of the Prime Minister)
findings.summary: The government signed a non-binding MOU with Hummingbird AI Holdings for a 150 MW AI data-centre campus, potentially expandable by 500 MW, with initial commercial operation proposed for Q1 2028; no construction reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us on the proposed owner-operator's incorporation (Delaware); its founder, Marc Farrell, is reported as linked to T&T conglomerate Massy, so beneficial control may be partly domestic. DCD notes the firm has little public footprint. Government cites ~US$5bn for three projects combined; no per-project value, so null. Tier 1: MOU only. Signing date inferred as Friday 10 July from AP and Guardian.

findings.controller: Not established (EY with unnamed third-party developers)
findings.local_actor: Government of Trinidad and Tobago (Office of the Prime Minister)
findings.summary: The government signed a non-binding MOU with Ernst & Young (US) for a 300 MW data centre to be developed with third-party developers, plus a framework for large-scale data-centre collaboration; no site, value or construction reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: EY is an adviser/convenor and the future owner-operator is unnamed; if EY-led US developers own it the pole would be us. Debe is reported as a candidate special economic zone. Tier 1: MOU only.

findings.controller: Government of Trinidad and Tobago (Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence)
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence (formerly Ministry of Digitalisation)
findings.summary: A government-owned Tier 4 data centre begun in 2022, funded by a US$120m CAF loan, had its site leased for 20 years in December 2025, civil works due to finish June 2026, and equipment reportedly already procured; location undisclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator is the state, so domestic. Tier 4 for construction under way (civil works). CAF loan is financier and does not set pole; the loan amount is not the facility value, so values null. 2023 tender named Phoenix Park Industrial Estate; current site undisclosed. IT equipment vendors unnamed. Single opened S3 source citing December 2025 procurement notices.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Public Administration and Artificial Intelligence; Ministry of Education
findings.summary: Ministers of Public Administration and Education signed a partnership agreement launching Future Ready TT, deploying ChatGPT tools (and Grammarly) in education and the public service, after a 550-licence pilot; T&T was in OpenAI's first Education for Countries cohort.
findings.analyst_inference: Model used through OpenAI's service, so pole us; no locally controlled weights. Tier 2: framework partnership plus pilot; no contract value or licence count for the full rollout. The agreement itself is sourced only to the state broadcaster (S4); TechNewsTT confirms only cohort membership. Whether OpenAI signed the May agreement directly is not stated.

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchase or vendor named in data-centre reporting

applications.null_reason: one search found TSTT's 2015 national CCTV expansion (800 cameras, four command centres) but no equipment vendor named; no Huawei/Hikvision safe-city system found

power.null_reason: no AI-specific power plant found; reporting raises grid (2.4 GW) and water concerns for proposed campuses only

research_gaps: Current RAN/core vendors for bmobile (TSTT) 4G/5G and Digicel; whether Huawei remains TSTT's 5G supplier and any Phoenix Park Huawei 5G deployment.
Equipment vendors and current site of the CAF-funded government Tier 4 data centre; operational status after June 2026 civil-works deadline.
Beneficial ownership of Hummingbird AI Holdings LLC and progress beyond the July 2026 MOU (due diligence, site, power and water agreements).
Owner-operator of the EY-convened 300 MW data centre and whether any binding agreement followed.
Text and counterparties of the May 2026 Future Ready TT agreement (signed with OpenAI directly?) and licence numbers.
Vendor of the TSTT-delivered national police CCTV network (2015, 1,673 cameras).
Any instrument from T&T's February 2026 AI engagement with India (none named in reporting).
